prompt_md: Buses come completely at random, one every 10 minutes on average, with no timetable. You turn up at a random time. On average, how many minutes do you wait?
prompt_short: Random buses, one every 10 min on average. Your average wait?
hint_md: The buses don't remember when the last one came.
explain_intuition_md: Random arrivals have no memory: however long it's been since the last bus, the next is still 10 minutes away on average. Halving to 5 only works for a perfectly regular timetable. With random gaps, you're also more likely to arrive during a long gap than a short one.
explain_math_md: Gaps are exponential with mean $10$, which is memoryless, so $E[\text{wait}] = 10$.
